tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

miri-2022-single-laser-model-class-a: Section 2.A, Eq. (1), p.2: the authors state their own single-laser model and say it represents a class-A laser.
miri-2022-eq6-continuous-not-stationary: Section 3.A, p.4-5: the paper states that Eq. (6) does not guarantee a continuous pattern is a stationary point. Section 3.B says the modified Hamiltonian demands complex, non-reciprocal coupling, which supports the second clause. Wording 'needs' is slightly stronger than 'is possible by utilizing'.
miri-2022-modified-hamiltonian-eq7: Section 3.B, Eq. (7), p.5: the paper defines its modified energy function with complex weights. The 'can be trained to store multiple patterns' clause is the stated purpose, tested later by simulation.
miri-2022-pseudoinverse-learning-rule: Section 3.B, Eq. (8), p.5: the paper defines its learning rule W = C(I - AA+) from the condition WA = 0, and the choice C = I. The derivation is one line (AA+A = A).
miri-2022-identical-oscillator-assumptio: Section 4, p.6: the paper states that its results assume identical oscillators and the class-A model, and that practical lasers differ (detuning, class B).
miri-2022-open-problems: Section 4, p.6: the paper states that full capacity in other architectures and functions remains to be examined, and calls its pseudoinverse learning simplistic.
scope-optical-optimizer-proposal: Abstract, p.1: the authors state what they explore (an optical optimizer with SFG and/or TPA, Zeno constraints, linear protocol for MIS).
fig12-simulation-setup: Figure 12 caption, p.23 (with Section 5.2): graph, Rtot = 20 pi, gadget parameters, 99% success criterion and ideal driving are stated by the authors.
tpa-lindbladian-definition: Section 2.1, p.5, Eq. (1): the paper defines the TPA Lindbladian and shows its action on zero, one and two photon states.
single-rail-encoding-definition: Section 3, p.8: the paper defines the single-rail encoding and says other states count as failure.
hom-constraint-gadget: Section 3.2, p.13, Eqs. (22) to (28): the paper derives the rotated Lindbladian step by step, with the condition of at most one photon per mode, and shows it equals the generator for sending |1j1k> to |0j0k>. The derivation is in the paper.
critical-damping-no-phase-inversion: Appendix B, p.32, Eqs. (45) to (52): the paper derives the damped oscillator ODE for rho12 at c = 0 and its three regimes. The critical-damping solution (1 + eta t/4) exp(-eta t/4) has no sign change. The non-Markovian remark is qualitative but follows from the non-exponential form.
appendix-b-damped-oscillator: Appendix B, p.31, Eqs. (45) to (50): the ODE is derived from the SFG Hamiltonian and loss by eliminating rho1p, under the stated condition c = 0, and the three regimes follow from the discriminant. Checked: the elimination is correct.
annealing-schedule-constant-rotation: Section 4.1, p.16, Eqs. (38) to (40): the paper defines the schedule it uses, with constant total rotation per step.
sparse-graph-compilation-open: Section 4.2, p.19: the paper states that reordering for sparser graphs is a non-trivial compilation problem beyond its scope.
qubo-extension-lossless-pump: Appendix A.2, pp.30-31: the paper states the lossless pump condition for QUBO and that it will not examine these protocols further. The condition is asserted, not derived, but it is stated as a limit of the extension.
scope-ideal-setting-no-photon-loss: Section 7.1, p.27: the paper states it worked in an idealized setting and ignored qubit-mode photon loss and partial distinguishability.
error-mitigation-not-fully-analyzed: Section 8, p.28: the paper states that the photon-loss mitigation scheme is not fully analyzed.
fast-switching-requirement-future-work: Section 8, p.28 (with Section 4.2): the paper names fast switching in the time-domain encoding as a requirement it would like to relax.
small-instances-three-and-five-node: Section 2.3, p.7, Eqs. (12), (13): the paper states the two test instances and their maximum independent sets. I checked both by hand.
numerical-methods-and-code: Section 6, p.25: the paper states its software, public code and data, laptop hardware and the 24 hour runtime.
hilbert-space-truncation: Figure 10 caption, p.20 (repeated in Figure 11): truncation at 10 photons for gamma < 10 and 5 above, and the pump space limit.
appendix-d-matrix-exponential-methods: Appendix D, pp.34-36: the paper states expm and expm_multiply and the binary decomposition with m = 30. Eq. (58) gives the O(tmax/2^m) accuracy.
noh-nn-setup-2-4-body-hamiltonian: Abstract and Section 2.3, Eq. (5), p.7: the paper states its own model, with beta and gamma scaling the 2-body and 4-body terms.
noh-nn-appendix-a-approximations: Appendix A, pp.16-17: the paper states the assumptions under which it derives the optical mapping (phase matching, undepleted pump, uniform amplitude, near axis).
noh-nn-experimental-apparatus: Section 3, Fig. 3, pp.8-10: laser, filter, EDFA power, SLM array, PPLN crystal at the Fourier plane, photodiodes, DAQ and MATLAB loop are all stated by the authors.
noh-nn-slm-speed-limits-testing: Section 3 p.9 (300 ms) and Section 4.1 p.10: the paper states that SLM speed makes larger tests time-prohibitive, and the capacity ratio is given as a bound (>= 10).
noh-nn-run-conditions: Section 4, p.10: the paper states delta = 0.20, N = 100, T = N, and beta, gamma for the two runs, and why gamma is large.
noh-nn-update-rule-monte-carlo: Section 2.2 p.4 and Section 2.3, Fig. 1, p.7: the paper defines its Monte Carlo retrieval, accept if delta H < 0, and the masking by flipping (Section 2.1).
noh-nn-retrieval-criterion-definition: Section 2.2, Eq. (4), pp.4-5: the paper defines successful recall, tau and the retrieval accuracy.
noh-nn-critical-capacity-definition: Section 2.2, p.5: the paper defines Kc as the maximum K with eta = 1.
noh-nn-correlated-simulation-setup: Section 4.2, Fig. 5, p.11: T = 100, 50 trials per (K, rho) pair, and the 2-body and 4-body maps are stated. The value omits beta and gamma for the maps, which does not change it.
noh-nn-average-correlation-definition: Appendix B Eq. (B13) p.18 and Appendix C: the paper defines the average correlation and the generation by Gaussian sampling, binarization and a tolerance loop (Listing 1, tolerance 1e-4).
noh-nn-mnist-setup: Section 4.3, p.12-13 and Appendix D.1: the paper states how patterns are chosen, the bicubic resize to 10 x 10, rho about 0.22 and within-class values up to 0.7.
qboost-qubo-baseline-formulation: Section 3.1, Eq. (4), p.335: the paper defines its own baseline objective.
region-count-upper-bound-conservative: Section 3.2, Eqs. (6), (7), pp.336-337: the paper states that no closed form is available for N >= 4 and that its bound is conservative.
region-count-footnote-scope: Footnote 2, p.336: the paper states that it ignores the case where a hyperplane becomes a solution space, and gives its probability as O(S/2^(2N)).
weights-low-bit-depth-scope: Section 3.1, p.335: the paper states that the bit-depth condition is shown for binary features only and that more general features are harder to analyze.
lambda-chosen-by-cross-validation: Section 4, p.339: the paper states that it picks lambda by validation error.
qboost-algorithm1-inner-loop-definition: Algorithm 1 and Section 5, p.340: the paper defines the inner loop step by step, as the value states.
qboost-algorithm2-outer-loop-definition: Algorithm 2 and Section 5, pp.340-341: the paper defines the outer loop as the value states, and describes it as freezing the earlier classifier.
experiment-scope-three-data-sets: Section 6, p.341: the paper states that it uses three data sets, two toy problems with a classical stand-in and one hard problem on a 52 qubit chip.
datasets-synthetic-and-eye-setup: Section 6.1, p.341: the paper states the synthetic mixture, the eye data features, and the 2 x 10^4 vectors split three ways.
classical-experiment-tabu-stumps-setup: Section 6.1, p.341: Tabu search, dw = 1 and the stump dictionary are stated. The counts 930 (M = 30) and 9312 (M = 96) check against the formula 2(M + M(M-1)/2).
hardware-car-detector-setup: Section 6.2, p.343: the paper states the car detector task, the Rainier chip, Q = 52, set sizes and patch count.
hardware-cascade-integration-setup: Section 6.2, p.343: the paper states the cascade integration, Q fixed at 52, algorithm use by stage, and the 50% false positive principle.
qmc-indirect-gap-measurement-method: Section 7, pp.344-345: the paper states its QMC method, what the measured quantity bounds, and the assumption on V01.
qmc-scaling-representativeness-limit: Section 7, p.345: the paper states that one cannot judge how typical the data set and scaling behavior are, and that scaling depends on the input.
conclusion-hardware-gain-not-established: Section 8, p.346: the paper states that hardware access is needed to establish the gain and that more qubits are needed.
dqrng-problem-statement-drng: Introduction, p.1-2: the paper defines the dRNG problem and the properties required of its numbers.
dqrng-notation-and-network-assumptions: Construction, p.3: the paper defines N, k, R, l, B, Rc, Rq, Rqc and F with R = F(Rqc).
dqrng-setup-assumptions-no-authenticatio: Construction, p.3: the paper states the quantum network, common basis and no authentication or encryption assumptions.
dqrng-network-architecture-beamsplitter: Model, pp.2-3: the paper states the physical layers, the N-to-N beamsplitter, Pnum = N(N-1)/2 and the reference signal of period T.
dqrng-step1-reveal-consensus-1: Construction, step 1, p.3: the paper defines the step as the value states.
dqrng-step2-3-quantum-measurement-and-re: Construction, steps 2 and 3, pp.3-4: the paper defines these steps as the value states.
dqrng-step4-5-consensus-2-and-output: Construction, steps 4 and 5, p.4: the paper defines Ifinal, Rqc and the output R = F(Rqc) as the value states.
dqrng-experimental-setup-hardware: Methods, pp.6-7: the paper states the lasers, wavelengths, PPLN waveguides, beamsplitters, SNSPDs, TDC and the 10 MHz reference.
dqrng-experiment-timing-binning: Figure 7 caption, p.7: the paper states jitters of 33 ps (detector) and 20 ps (converter) and the 250 ps bin width.
dqrng-stated-limits-and-text-gaps: Methods, p.8 and Introduction, p.2: the paper states that one SPDC source lowers the correlated rate, that the average rate is rather low, and that the protocol produces one or a small set of numbers at a time.

theory_low.miri-2022-single-laser-threshold-seeding: Section 2.A, p.2: the stability change at g0 > 1 and the seeding phase lock are stated without a derivation in the text; an analytic property asserted, not proved.
theory_low.miri-2022-hebbian-weights-binary-local-m: Methods 5.B, pp.7-8: the Hessian is written out, but positive semidefiniteness is called 'straightforward' and rests on Ref. [33] (Chung, spectral graph theory). Not written out in the paper. Semidefinite Hessian also does not by itself prove a strict local minimum.
theory_low.miri-2022-weight-matrix-rank-hermitian: Section 3.B, p.5: the rank claim is asserted, not proved. W = I - AA+ is a projector onto the orthogonal complement of the span of A, so its rank is n - k, not k. The n x k element count and Hermiticity are called 'straightforward' with no proof. Value repeats a questionable claim.
theory_low.critical-sfg-nonmarkovian: Section 5.1, p.21: an interpretive remark explaining a numerical result. No definition of non-Markovianity is given. Appendix B derives only the rho12 decay at c = 0 (Eq. 52, non-exponential) and does not prove the general statement.
theory_low.sfg-phase-flip-and-loss: Section 2.2, p.6 (also 5.2): the two-level Rabi mapping between |2,0p> and |0,1p> and the timing values are stated without derivation, in a Background section the paper says has no original results. The text layer also garbles the time values.
theory_low.zeno-blockade-driving-effective-x: Section 3.1, p.9, Eqs. (14) to (17): the reduction is stated as approximate for gamma/c >> 1, argued informally, with no error bound; checked only numerically (Figure 3).
theory_low.full-phase-flip-insufficient-constraint: Section 3.3, p.14: 'not sufficient' and the leakage mechanism are asserted qualitatively. No proof or counterexample is given; the section says it will discuss it later and only restates it.
theory_low.digitized-transverse-ising-adiabatic: Section 4.1, p.15: an informal appeal to the adiabatic theorem and an approximation (Eq. 37, small phi and c). No bound or proof is given.
theory_low.fully-connected-delay-protocol: Appendix C, p.34: Algorithm 1 is given with the claim that every pair can interact, supported only by an example figure (Figure 18, n = 5). No proof for general n.
theory_low.noh-nn-optical-mapping-signal-sh: Section 2.3 and Appendix A, pp.16-17: the mapping is derived under stated approximations (undepleted pump, phase matching, near axis, uniform Gaussian amplitude) and is not a proved theorem. The paper does not test the mapping separately.
theory_low.qboost-bit-depth-lower-bound: Section 3.2, Eqs. (6) to (8), pp.336-337: an informal counting argument. It assumes each region holds a lattice vertex, uses an upper bound on region count, and a Stirling-type step marked with an approximation sign. No theorem, no full proof. The value states it as a derived result.
theory_low.hyperplane-region-counts-small-n: Figure 1 caption, p.336: the counts 14, 104 and 1882 are stated in a caption with no derivation or code. Eq. (6) is a formula, not a computation of these numbers.
theory_low.weak-lambda-regime-thinning-argument: Section 4, p.338: an informal derivation with the threshold formula garbled in the text layer. The VC statement follows from cited bounds (Eqs. 10, 11). Not a theorem with a proof.
theory_low.dqrng-correctness-argument-four-parties: Analysis, Correctness, p.4: labelled a proof but is an informal argument for one four-party case with one honest party. No probability bound, and the general claim for any N is not proved. The argument also does not show unpredictability of Ifinal beyond asserting it.
